title: Home Energy Tax Credits 2026: What Expired and What's Left
summary: Explains which home energy tax credits the July 2025 budget law ended (25C, 25D, EV credits) and what survived into 2026 (IRA rebates, state and utility programs, the EV charger credit to mid-2026).

assertions.quote: And critically, it also covered efficient heating and cooling equipment, including heat pumps.
the tax credit for heat pumps expired, but the rebate program for heat pumps survived

verdicts.note: The 25C credit was terminated for property placed in service after December 31, 2025 by the July 2025 budget law.

assertions.quote: the appliance rebate program, which pays you up to $14,000 to install efficient equipment like heat pumps

verdicts.note: The IRA electrification rebates are limited to households under 150% of area median income and many states had not launched them, so most homeowners cannot get them.

assertions.quote: administered by each individual state and they are rolling out across the country throughout 2026.

verdicts.note: HEAR rebates are run by state energy offices and only a minority of states had launched programs by 2025.

assertions.quote: Your state and local programs and your utility company rebates were not touched by this federal law at all.

verdicts.note: State and utility programs are funded separately (ratepayers, state budgets) and the budget law did not repeal them.

assertions.quote: Work that was finished during 2025 still counts.

verdicts.note: The 25C repeal applies to property placed in service after 2025, so 2025 installations remain eligible on 2025 returns.
IRS: the 25C credit is disallowed only for property placed in service after December 31, 2025, so a heat pump placed in service in 2025 remains eligible.
IRS 25C page: the credit can be claimed for improvements made through December 31, 2025, and is claimed for the tax year the property is installed.

assertions.quote: It also covered home battery storage systems, geothermal heat pumps, small wind systems, and more.

verdicts.note: The 25D residential clean energy credit, which covered geothermal heat pumps, ends for expenditures after December 31, 2025.

IRS: the 25D residential clean energy credit is not allowed for expenditures after December 31, 2025, and an expenditure counts only when installation is completed; geothermal heat pumps fall under 25D, though this fact sheet does not name them or the 30% rate.
